p1c1.caption: before the first cut
p1c1.title: Introduction
p1c1.rationale: Author's eye before the kaleidoscope: one uncut slate lens; the served heading stays a heads-up display, Churchill's self-mockery and the June-4 set-piece carry shard-tick quotes, the impossible-summing-up closer is the coda.

p2c1.rationale: Heroic myth ascendant; biggest shards in the book (prototype).
p2c1.title: Churchill as Liberty’s Champion: Heroic View

p2c10.caption: nothing else but ambition to cling to
p2c10.title: Churchill’s Desire for Fame: His Motive
p2c10.rationale: Grasping talons: fame-lust shards reach upward, clutching (¶1, ¶4, ¶5). Curved vermilion claws on lampblack — distinct from p2c1's straight ochre monoliths and p2c2's mirror. Vermilion occluders are motif-native. Closes Part II. Thesis ¶1 with vermilion claw-mark, Savrola/Macaulay close ¶8 as quote.

p2c2.rationale: Prosecution mirror — same shard set inverted, Vermilion relight (C2).
p2c2.title: Churchill as Failed Statesman: Critical View

p2c3.caption: seventy names hung like stars
p2c3.title: Churchill’s Contemporaries: Whom He Knew
p2c3.rationale: Constellation pins: ~70 acquaintances (¶2–36) as a social star-chart on a lampblack night bed. Salon-wall register reading; split continuations ¶10/11 and ¶23/24 glued AS SERVED via label hooks.

p2c4.caption: the afternoon of May the twenty-eighth
p2c4.title: Churchill’s Finest Hour—May 28, 1940: The Decisive Moment
p2c4.rationale: Converging wedge: all blades aim at the vermilion afternoon (¶2, ¶9, ¶13). Left-weighted convergence, numeral right — inverse of p2c8. Cabinet vow ¶16 and beaches peroration ¶21 as speeches, confidential memo ¶18 as memo slip, wept coda ¶22, never-surrender thesis ¶23.

p2c5.caption: for and against, in perfect balance
p2c5.title: Churchill as Leader: Suited to High Office?
p2c5.rationale: Balanced scales: equipoise diptych — the book's only symmetric plate. For (¶0–6) vs Against (¶7–12) with opposing verdict plaques ¶6 / ¶12.

p2c6.caption: words are the only things which last for ever
p2c6.title: Churchill’s Genius with Words: His Greatest Strength
p2c6.rationale: Type-as-shards: letterforms cut into ochre facets — W/O/R for WORDS (¶1, ¶12). Lampblack letters on ochre (~7:1). Japan declaration letter ¶6–10, tools broadcast ¶13, central thesis ¶19, verdict close ¶23.

p2c7.caption: seventy-seven tiles of exact words
p2c7.title: Churchill’s Eloquence: His Exact Words
p2c7.rationale: 77 small tiles: eloquence as mosaic — scattered rotated diamonds in mixed hues (not the strict ledger grid of p4c2). Strict setup/quote two-voice with dated rail from data-fw-label dates. Four wartime set-pieces as full-bleed plates: ¶47, ¶51–52, ¶55, ¶58.

p2c8.caption: a cigar, a gesture, a suit of blue
p2c8.title: Churchill in Symbols: Metonymy
p2c8.rationale: Three swift strokes: cigar/V-sign/uniform (¶2, ¶4/5/6) as three PARALLEL calligraphic blades — parallel, not p2c4's convergence. Numeral left, strokes right. Emblem tags on ¶4/5/6 plus ¶9 drink as fourth tag; thesis ¶2; coda ¶10.

p2c9.caption: true, like a ship's compass
p2c9.title: Churchill, True: In a Single Word
p2c9.rationale: One word-stone: True single engraved block (¶1, ¶6). Bone block and Bone numeral kept DISJOINT — number left, stone right. Oaken Heart quotations ¶5–9 as engraved blocks, Shakespeare verse ¶4 as centered inscription, lead ¶3 as setup.

p3c10.caption: tears not of sorrow but of wonder
p3c10.rationale: Softest geometry in the book — curves only: one held tear answered by a smaller witness tear; lampblack ellipse occluders (prototype-p3c7 precedent); wonder point in ochre.
p3c10.title: Churchill in Tears: Telling Detail

p3c2.caption: sufficient for himself
p3c2.rationale: Disdain as composition — all mass turned away left while the numeral is exiled right; one escaping bone tooth is the unheeded world; Part-III candlelight tick at the far edge.
p3c2.title: Churchill’s Disdain: His Dominant Quality

p3c3.caption: my policy is, 'Fight on.'
p3c3.rationale: Sharpest angles in the book — vermilion blades bare left-to-right, the fourth pointing back (war cuts both ways); a slate tooth grounds the cost of war; lampblack bed for maximum attack.
p3c3.title: Churchill’s Belligerence: His Defining Characteristic

p3c4.caption: 1874–1965, with milestones missing
p3c4.rationale: The conventional time line fails — the plate marches anyway, ledger shards ascending 1874→1965 toward the numeral; the 1940 beat burns vermilion; ochre year ticks bracket the life. Ledger index OFF (S3): one head needs no navigation.
p3c4.title: Churchill’s Time Line: Key Events

p3c5.caption: the ever-absent father
p3c5.rationale: LEFT half of the father/son hinge: the ochre shard clipped at x=600, bone zigzag split edge with hinge pin; the son's unanswered letter reaches across the split from the missing half's side; numeral looks right toward the father.
p3c5.title: Churchill as Son: His Most Formative Role

p3c6.caption: two verdicts, one household
p3c6.rationale: RIGHT half of the hinge, completed — byte-identical shard transform, opposite clip, mirrored numeral gazing left at the son; verdict diptych tiles (bone Good / slate Not Good) echo the two heads; slate shadow is the cold father.
p3c6.title: Churchill as Father: A Good Parent?

p3c7.rationale: Painter: wettest colour, impasto grain at max (prototype).
p3c7.title: Churchill the Painter: His Favorite Pastime

p3c8.caption: earn a fortune, spend a larger one
p3c8.rationale: Cracked vermilion vessel center; one SMALL ochre inflow (earned by writing) against five LARGER spilling teeth, the last bleeding off the plate edge — inflow < outflow, literally; gallery occluders on the lampblack bed.
p3c8.title: Churchill the Spendthrift: A Weakness

p3c9.caption: contradictory conclusions
p3c9.rationale: Every tile a hue — 36 witness tiles in flanking banks, no two adjacent tiles agreeing, center aisle holding only numeral + occluders; the 57 witnesses live in the fully-mapped body (19 setup / 18 quote / 18 caption); no coda — the collage refuses to sum up.
p3c9.title: Conflicting Views of Churchill: How Others Saw Him

p4c1.caption: a glass of weak whisky
p4c1.rationale: Prosecution/defense diptych over the drinking record: WAS [0] vs WAS NOT [6] verdict plaques frame the evidence; the spirit-level plate breaks between them.
p4c1.title: Churchill the Drinker: An Alcoholic?

p4c10.caption: He never resigned himself
p4c10.rationale: Part IV's closing benediction: a single coda para under theme's Way-40-rhyme only-child base, given colophon air; the faded slate plate is the Empire's afterimage.
p4c10.title: Churchill’s Empire: How He Saw the World

p4c2.rationale: 109 fact-paras: calmest plate, tabular tiles; index map from Cohort C engineer.
p4c2.title: Churchill in Context: Facts at a Glance

p4c3.caption: too interesting to ignore
p4c3.rationale: A decorousness argument under a slate veil: the blunt thesis [4] is the chapter's only raised voice; rumors [8–9] and the Asquith/Lawrence counterfactual [11] stay veiled in calm prose.
p4c3.title: Churchill and Sex: Too Interesting to Ignore

p4c4.caption: my precious charming Clemmie
p4c4.rationale: Marriage diptych: happy [0] / not-happy [7] verdict plaques; the March-1916 letters [4–5] set as correspondence; the two photograph captions [11,13] in sepia caption voice.
p4c4.title: Churchill as Husband: A Happy Marriage?

p4c5.caption: this sceptred isle
p4c5.rationale: Myth essay cresting in Shakespeare: eleven verse lines [9–19] set as a centered stanza block, the refusal-to-believe coda [20] as benediction, the Liberty/Empire contradiction [4–5] left to argue in calm prose.
p4c5.title: Churchill’s Island Story: His Myth

p4c6.caption: Remember Winston Churchill
p4c6.rationale: Gallery hang in prose: setup [0] then 18 numbered captions [1–18] on a dated rail with frame-edge ticks echoing the plate's 6×3 sepia hang, aging light→dark down the page.
p4c6.title: Churchill in Photographs: How He Changed Through Time

p4c7.caption: less a personality than a personification
p4c7.rationale: Fiction's devices applied to a life: the bulldog/Woom unconvincing-character passage [4] as the central exhibit (quote), the ironies catalogue [6] and symbol exploitation [11] as calm accumulation, closing in the mythic-scale coda [12].
p4c7.title: Churchill as the Hero of a Novel: The Imagined and the Real

p4c8.caption: walking with Destiny
p4c8.rationale: Survival catalogue [5–14] as a quickened ledger rhythm (list-items with date-beat energy), destiny's own voice [15,17–18] as set-piece quotes, Halifax/Chamberlain [20–26] as calm forensic prose, closing in the double-edged coda [27].
p4c8.title: Churchill’s Destiny: How He Saw Himself

p4c9.caption: the clattering down
p4c9.rationale: The cause stated, evidenced, and cracked: constituent letters/speeches [5,10,14–15] in correspondence/oration voice, the replacement-Empire thesis [11–13] as display argument, the clattering-down coda [17–19] as falling close.
p4c9.title: Churchill the Imperialist: His Cause

p5c1.caption: seventeen hundred messages across the water
p5c1.title: Churchill and Roosevelt: Friends as Well as Allies?
p5c1.rationale: True diptych: warm-case half (Had a Warm Friendship) vs cold-case half (Did Not Have a Warm Friendship); served verdict heads oppose each other; Atlantic cable-pair plate spans both.

p5c10.rationale: Epitaph: one point of light; 63 words; colophon finish (C6).
p5c10.title: Remember Winston Churchill: Epitaph

p5c2.caption: he looked backward, not forward
p5c2.title: Churchill’s Imagination: How He Saw History
p5c2.rationale: Backward-gaze thesis: Blenheim Victory Column inscription as monumental centered verse; the Admiralty-flag memo as a dispatch; the Oran 'I leave it to history' appeal inside ¶29 stays served prose (too long to lift).

p5c4.caption: one layer peeled back
p5c4.title: Churchill Exposed: Missing Information Supplied
p5c4.rationale: Suppressed-material dossier: calm bone record, the Barnum 'Boneless Wonder' set-piece as the chapter's one shard-tick quote, the Both-verdict closer as thesis.

p5c5.caption: sixty-three statements, five of them false
p5c5.title: Churchill True or False: Challenged Assumptions
p5c5.rationale: True/False quiz: every even index 2..126 is a mask-q number row; served statement paras stay prose EXCEPT the 15 served-quotation statements (48–63 block + lead-in ¶97) which carry quote styling; answers para is mask-a inside the keyboard-honest details disclosure (facets.js wraps it; C5).

p5c6.title: The Tragedy of Winston Churchill, Englishman: The Meaning of His Life

p5c7.caption: the portrait he hated
p5c7.title: Churchill in Portrait: A Likeness
p5c7.rationale: Portrait-trial: the two served photo captions close the chapter as gallery captions; the aeroplane-in-the-dusk self-portrait inside ¶7 stays served prose; hated-portrait plate voids the face.

p5c8.caption: the tide goes out; the tablet remains
p5c8.title: Churchill’s Last Days: How He Died
p5c8.rationale: Death-elegy: last-words line and Abbey tablet as centered epitaph pair; the backward-sliding memory pageant (¶6) stays calm prose; ebbing-tide plate sinks below the numeral.

p5c9.caption: the verdict is yours; the chair is empty
p5c9.title: My Churchill: Judgment
p5c9.rationale: Reader-verdict: the direct-address summons opens as thesis, the quarterdeck vision (cigar, flags, tears) centers as the book's emotional epitaph pair, the see-clearer closer is the coda; judgment-seat plate leaves the chair empty.
